quests.instruction: Sphere, Cube, Sphere, Cube, Sphere, ___? What comes next in this pattern of solid shapes?
quests.question: Cube
quests.hint: Look at how Sphere and Cube keep taking turns — which one comes right after Sphere?
quests.explanation: This pattern alternates Sphere, Cube, so after Sphere comes Cube again.
quests.funFact: Patterns can be built from solid 3D shapes too, not just flat 2D ones.

quests.instruction: Which shape shares the exact same 4 lines of symmetry as a square, because it's really just a square standing on its point?
quests.question: Diamond
quests.hint: Think back — this shape is simply a square, tilted to balance on one corner.
quests.explanation: A diamond has the same 4 lines of symmetry as a square, since it's really the same shape just turned.
quests.funFact: Turning a shape never changes how many lines of symmetry it has.

quests.instruction: Star, Heart, Star, Heart, Star, ___? What comes next in this pattern?
quests.question: Heart
quests.hint: Follow the back-and-forth between Star and Heart to find what comes next.
quests.explanation: This pattern alternates Star, Heart. The sequence just ended on Star, so Heart comes next.
quests.funFact: Alternating patterns are predictable because they only ever use two shapes, taking turns.

quests.instruction: Hexagon, Hexagon, Octagon, Octagon, Hexagon, Hexagon, Octagon, Octagon, ___? What comes next in this pattern?
quests.question: Hexagon
quests.hint: This pattern repeats Hexagon, Hexagon, Octagon, Octagon over and over — count carefully to see where you are.
quests.explanation: This pattern repeats Hexagon, Hexagon, Octagon, Octagon. The sequence just finished a full group ending in two Octagons, so a new group begins with Hexagon.
quests.funFact: Pattern puzzles like this help build sharp attention to detail.

quests.instruction: Pentagon, Hexagon, Octagon, Pentagon, Hexagon, Octagon, Pentagon, Hexagon, ___? What comes next in this pattern?
quests.question: Octagon
quests.hint: This pattern repeats Pentagon, Hexagon, Octagon over and over — count carefully to see where you are.
quests.explanation: This pattern repeats Pentagon, Hexagon, Octagon. The sequence just gave Pentagon, Hexagon — so Octagon completes the group.
quests.funFact: This pattern uses shapes in order of their side count: 5, then 6, then 8.

quests.instruction: Oval, Oval, Circle, Oval, Oval, Circle, Oval, ___? What comes next in this pattern?
quests.question: Oval
quests.hint: This pattern repeats Oval, Oval, Circle over and over — count carefully to see where you are.
quests.explanation: This pattern repeats Oval, Oval, Circle. The sequence just gave one Oval to start a new group, so a second Oval comes next.
quests.funFact: Careful counting is the key to solving any repeating pattern.

quests.instruction: Hexagon, Pentagon, Hexagon, Pentagon, Hexagon, ___? What comes next in this pattern?
quests.question: Pentagon
quests.hint: Look at how Hexagon and Pentagon keep taking turns — which one comes right after Hexagon?
quests.explanation: This pattern alternates Hexagon, Pentagon, so after Hexagon comes Pentagon again.
quests.funFact: Even shapes with lots of sides can be used in simple alternating patterns.

quests.instruction: Cube, Pyramid, Cube, Pyramid, Cube, ___? What comes next in this pattern of solid shapes?
quests.question: Pyramid
quests.hint: Follow the back-and-forth between Cube and Pyramid to find what comes next.
quests.explanation: This pattern alternates Cube, Pyramid, so after Cube comes Pyramid again.
quests.funFact: Alternating solid-shape patterns work exactly the same way as flat-shape patterns.

quests.instruction: Cone, Cube, Sphere, Cone, Cube, Sphere, Cone, Cube, ___? What comes next in this pattern of solid shapes?
quests.question: Sphere
quests.hint: Break this into groups of Cone, Cube, Sphere to spot what comes next.
quests.explanation: This pattern repeats Cone, Cube, Sphere, so after Cone, Cube comes Sphere again.
quests.funFact: Three-shape patterns work the same way whether the shapes are flat or solid.

quests.instruction: Square, Square, Triangle, Triangle, Square, Square, Triangle, Triangle, ___? What comes next in this pattern?
quests.question: Square
quests.hint: This pattern repeats Square, Square, Triangle, Triangle over and over — count carefully to see where you are.
quests.explanation: This pattern repeats Square, Square, Triangle, Triangle, so after two triangles comes a square to start the next group.
quests.funFact: Patterns with pairs of matching shapes are a fun variation on simple alternating patterns.

quests.instruction: Pentagon, Star, Pentagon, Star, Pentagon, ___? What comes next in this pattern?
quests.question: Star
quests.hint: Follow the back-and-forth between Pentagon and Star to find what comes next.
quests.explanation: This pattern alternates Pentagon, Star. The sequence just ended on Pentagon, so Star comes next.
quests.funFact: Remember, a pentagon and a 5-pointed star are closely related — a pentagon hides inside every star!

quests.instruction: Square, Triangle, Triangle, Square, Triangle, Triangle, Square, Triangle, ___? What comes next in this pattern?
quests.question: Triangle
quests.hint: Look for the repeating group of three: Square, Triangle, Triangle — then find your place in it.
quests.explanation: This pattern repeats Square, Triangle, Triangle, so after Square, Triangle comes another Triangle.
quests.funFact: Even a three-shape group can start to feel tricky if two of the shapes repeat inside it.

quests.instruction: Which shape, with its infinite lines of symmetry, could you use to end almost any symmetry pattern with total confidence?
quests.question: Circle
quests.hint: Think back to the very first symmetry lesson in this band — the shape that beats every other shape.
quests.explanation: A circle's infinite lines of symmetry make it the most symmetrical shape you've learned in this entire game.
quests.funFact: You've now learned that a regular shape's lines of symmetry usually match its sides — except for a circle, which simply has no limit.

quests.instruction: Cube, Sphere, Cone, Cylinder, Cube, Sphere, Cone, Cylinder, Cube, Sphere, ___? What comes next in this longer pattern of solid shapes?
quests.question: Cone
quests.hint: This pattern repeats Cube, Sphere, Cone, Cylinder over and over — count carefully to see where you are.
quests.explanation: This pattern repeats Cube, Sphere, Cone, Cylinder. The sequence just gave Cube, Sphere — so Cone comes next.
quests.funFact: Even a four-shape repeating pattern is easy to solve once you spot the full group.

quests.instruction: Circle, Crescent, Circle, Crescent, Circle, ___? What comes next in this pattern?
quests.question: Crescent
quests.hint: Look at how Circle and Crescent keep taking turns — which one comes right after Circle?
quests.explanation: This pattern alternates Circle, Crescent, so after Circle comes Crescent again.
quests.funFact: This pattern looks a bit like the moon changing shape through its different phases!

quests.instruction: Sphere, Sphere, Cube, Sphere, Sphere, Cube, Sphere, Sphere, ___? What comes next in this pattern of solid shapes?
quests.question: Cube
quests.hint: Break this into groups of Sphere, Sphere, Cube to spot what comes next.
quests.explanation: This pattern repeats Sphere, Sphere, Cube, so after two spheres comes a cube.
quests.funFact: This same repeating trick works whether you're looking at flat shapes or solid ones.

quests.instruction: Cone, Cylinder, Cone, Cylinder, Cone, ___? What comes next in this pattern of solid shapes?
quests.question: Cylinder
quests.hint: This pattern swaps between Cone and Cylinder every single time.
quests.explanation: This pattern alternates Cone, Cylinder, so after Cone comes Cylinder again.
quests.funFact: Just like flat shapes, solid shapes can alternate back and forth in a simple pattern.

quests.instruction: Square, Diamond, Square, Diamond, Square, ___? What comes next in this pattern?
quests.question: Diamond
quests.hint: This pattern swaps between Square and Diamond every single time.
quests.explanation: This pattern alternates Square, Diamond, so after Square comes Diamond again.
quests.funFact: Remember, a diamond is really just a square standing on its point!

quests.instruction: Heart, Heart, Diamond, Diamond, Heart, Heart, Diamond, Diamond, ___? What comes next in this pattern?
quests.question: Heart
quests.hint: Look for the repeating group of four: Heart, Heart, Diamond, Diamond — then find your place in it.
quests.explanation: This pattern repeats Heart, Heart, Diamond, Diamond, so after two diamonds comes a heart to start the next group.
quests.funFact: Patterns that use pairs of shapes can feel extra fun and rhythmic.

quests.instruction: Square, Pentagon, Hexagon, Square, Pentagon, Hexagon, Square, Pentagon, ___? What comes next in this pattern?
quests.question: Hexagon
quests.hint: This pattern repeats Square, Pentagon, Hexagon over and over — count carefully to see where you are.
quests.explanation: This pattern repeats Square, Pentagon, Hexagon, so after Square, Pentagon comes Hexagon again.
quests.funFact: This pattern is extra fun because it also counts up in sides: 4, 5, then 6.

quests.instruction: Hexagon, Octagon, Hexagon, Octagon, Hexagon, Octagon, Hexagon, ___? What comes next in this pattern?
quests.question: Octagon
quests.hint: Follow the back-and-forth between Hexagon and Octagon to find what comes next.
quests.explanation: This pattern alternates Hexagon, Octagon, so after Hexagon comes Octagon again.
quests.funFact: Even after many repeats, an alternating pattern never changes its simple back-and-forth rule.

quests.instruction: Circle, Oval, Circle, Oval, Circle, ___? What comes next in this pattern?
quests.question: Oval
quests.hint: This pattern swaps between Circle and Oval every single time.
quests.explanation: This pattern alternates Circle, Oval. The sequence just ended on Circle, so Oval comes next.
quests.funFact: Even two similar curved shapes like circle and oval can form a clear alternating pattern.

quests.instruction: Square, Pentagon, Square, Pentagon, Square, Pentagon, Square, ___? What comes next in this final pattern?
quests.question: Pentagon
quests.hint: Look at how Square and Pentagon keep taking turns — which one comes right after Square?
quests.explanation: This pattern alternates Square, Pentagon, so after Square comes Pentagon again.
quests.funFact: You've now practiced spotting patterns with two shapes, three shapes, and even four shapes in a row!

quests.instruction: Cone, Pyramid, Cone, Pyramid, Cone, ___? What comes next in this pattern of solid shapes?
quests.question: Pyramid
quests.hint: This pattern swaps between Cone and Pyramid every single time.
quests.explanation: This pattern alternates Cone, Pyramid, so after Cone comes Pyramid again.
quests.funFact: Cones and pyramids are similar because they both narrow to a single point at the top.

quests.instruction: Which shape has only 2 lines of symmetry, even though it has 4 sides?
quests.question: Rectangle
quests.hint: Think about the shape where only the middle-straight folds match, not the corner-to-corner folds.
quests.explanation: A rectangle has only 2 lines of symmetry — straight down the middle each way — because its sides aren't all equal.
quests.funFact: Unlike a square, a rectangle's 4 sides don't all match, so it has fewer lines of symmetry than sides.

quests.instruction: Cube, Rectangular Prism, Cube, Rectangular Prism, Cube, ___? What comes next in this pattern of solid shapes?
quests.question: Rectangular Prism
quests.hint: This pattern swaps between Cube and Rectangular Prism every single time.
quests.explanation: This pattern alternates Cube, Rectangular Prism, so after Cube comes Rectangular Prism again.
quests.funFact: A cube and a rectangular prism are closely related, which makes a fun pattern pair.

quests.instruction: Cube, Cube, Sphere, Cube, Cube, Sphere, Cube, Cube, ___? What comes next in this final pattern of solid shapes?
quests.question: Sphere
quests.hint: Break this into groups of Cube, Cube, Sphere to spot what comes next.
quests.explanation: This pattern repeats Cube, Cube, Sphere, so after two cubes comes a sphere, just as it has every time before.
quests.funFact: Whether flat or solid, every pattern in this band followed the very same simple rule: find the repeating group, then continue it.

quests.instruction: Rectangle, Square, Rectangle, Square, Rectangle, ___? What comes next in this pattern?
quests.question: Square
quests.hint: Look at how Rectangle and Square keep taking turns — which one comes right after Rectangle?
quests.explanation: This pattern alternates Rectangle, Square. The sequence just ended on Rectangle, so Square comes next.
quests.funFact: Even two shapes that look similar, like rectangle and square, can make a clear pattern.

quests.instruction: Heart, Diamond, Star, Heart, Diamond, Star, Heart, Diamond, ___? What comes next in this pattern?
quests.question: Star
quests.hint: Look for the repeating group of three: Heart, Diamond, Star — then find your place in it.
quests.explanation: This pattern repeats Heart, Diamond, Star, so after Heart, Diamond comes Star again.
quests.funFact: Patterns with three different pointy shapes can be some of the trickiest to memorize.

quests.instruction: Circle, Circle, Square, Square, Triangle, Triangle, Circle, Circle, Square, Square, ___? What comes next in this longer pattern?
quests.question: Triangle
quests.hint: Look closely — this pattern repeats a group of six shapes, in pairs: circle, circle, square, square, triangle, triangle.
quests.explanation: This pattern repeats pairs of Circle, Square, Triangle, so after this pair of squares comes a pair of triangles.
quests.funFact: Longer patterns just combine simpler ideas — here, it's pairs of three different shapes.
